tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

delaySeconds.description: Seconds from now to wake up. Clamped to [60, 3600] by the runtime. Required unless `stop` is true.

reason.description: One short sentence explaining the chosen delay. Goes to telemetry and is shown to the user. Be specific. Required unless `stop` is true.

prompt.description: The /loop input to fire on wake-up. Pass the same /loop input verbatim each turn so the next firing re-enters the skill and continues the loop. For autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` instead (the dynamic-pacing variant, not the CronCreate-mode `<<autonomous-loop>>`). Required unless `stop` is true.

stop.description: Set to true to end the dynamic loop immediately instead of scheduling another wakeup. When true, all other fields are ignored and no further wakeups fire.

noop.description: true = nothing changed (you checked and there is nothing to report). false = something happened worth keeping (edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, surfaced a finding). Consecutive noop:true ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak. Required unless `stop` is true.

tools.name: SendFeedback
tools.description:
Use this tool to draft feedback about Claude Code when you hit a high-signal moment. That includes both PRODUCT issues and MODEL-BEHAVIOR issues:
- a reproducible tool or product failure was just resolved or abandoned
- the user clearly expressed frustration with Claude Code or with how you handled the task
- you hit a missing capability that blocked a reasonable request
- you notice, or the user points out, that your own behavior in this session went wrong, for example: you gave a confident answer then had to retract it; you stopped short and handed work back when you could have finished; you declined or disputed a reasonable request; you spawned more subagents than the task warranted; your tone was off; you asked more clarifying questions than needed; you expanded scope beyond what was asked

The draft is QUEUED LOCALLY. It is never sent without the user's explicit approval, and calling this tool renders no UI and does not interrupt the conversation, so never announce it or ask the user about it mid-task.

Write `details` as short labeled bullets in this exact order, one to three lines each, no narrative paragraphs:
- **What happened:** the observed behavior vs. what was expected, with exact error text if short. Facts only.
- **What the user said:** the user's own words that prompted this, quoted. If nothing did, write "User didn't comment; observed by the model." Never paraphrase sentiment into a stronger claim.
- **Repro:** the minimal steps or shape that reproduces it.
- **Evidence:** identifiers a reader can chase, such as request IDs, timestamps, file paths, versions. Omit the bullet if there are none.

Constraints:
- Never fabricate or exaggerate user sentiment; report only what actually happened.
- Everything in the draft must be sourced from the user or the session, never inferred: leave unknown fields blank rather than guess, and add a final **Cause:** bullet only for a root cause you verified in-session.
- Use `area` to name the part of Claude Code the feedback is about (a feature, command, or workflow, e.g. "hooks config", "/help", "file editing") when there is a clear one; leave it blank otherwise.
- Use `failure_mode` ONLY when the report is about model behavior (how Claude responded), not a product bug. Pick the single closest value, or `other` when it is a model-behavior issue that fits no listed value; omit the field only when the report is a product/tool bug with no model-behavior component.
- Use `task_category` to name what kind of task the session was doing, or `other` when it is a clear task that fits no listed value. Omit only if genuinely unclear.
- Do not include secrets or credentials. Refer to people by role ("a teammate", "the PR reviewer"), never by name, email address, or chat/user ID. This applies inside quoted user words too: replace a name or handle with a bracketed role (e.g. "[a teammate]") and keep the rest verbatim. Do not include customer-facing channel or DM IDs, or excerpts of customer content. Session, request, and run IDs, timestamps, repo/PR numbers, and file paths (written relative to the working directory, or ~-prefixed, not absolute paths under the user's home) remain the right evidence.
- If the issue looks like a security vulnerability: describe the class of problem, never a working exploit or step-by-step extraction path.
- Draft only at the natural moments listed above, and at most one draft per distinct issue; never re-draft the same issue in a session.

type.description: What kind of feedback this is.

title.description: Short, specific one-line summary of the issue.

details.description: Labeled bullets, in order: **What happened:** (observed vs. expected, exact error text if short); **What the user said:** (quoted, or "User didn't comment; observed by the model."); **Repro:** (minimal steps); **Evidence:** (request IDs, timestamps, paths, versions; omit if none); optionally a final **Cause:** only if verified in-session. One to three lines per bullet. No narrative paragraphs, no speculation, no secrets.

area.description: Optional short tag naming the part of Claude Code this is about (e.g. "hooks config", "/help", "file editing"). Leave blank if unclear.

failure_mode.description: When the report is about MODEL BEHAVIOR (not a product bug), the closest failure mode, or `other` when it is a model-behavior issue that fits no listed value. Omit only when the report is a product/tool bug with no model-behavior component.

task_category.description: What kind of task the session was doing when the issue occurred, or `other` when it is a clear task that fits no listed value. Omit only if genuinely unclear.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

skill.description: The name of a skill from the available-skills list. Do not guess names.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

query.description: Query to find deferred tools. Use "select:<tool_name>" for direct selection, or keywords to search.

max_results.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 5)

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with the same `scriptPath` instead of re-sending the full script. Takes precedence over `script` and `name`.

resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. Completed agent() calls with unchanged (prompt, opts) return their cached results instantly; only edited or new calls re-run. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

# module-to-process — Workflow (Steps 5–9)

Continues [`workflow.md`](workflow.md). Path variables, checkpoints and escalation: [`paths-and-state.md`](paths-and-state.md).

## Step 5 — Task sheets (sap-analyst, Opus)

1. Print the Step 5 line. Tasks = L4 rows of `step4.json` (approved) with kind `cbo`, `enh` or `ext`. None → skip with `(skipped — no CBO / enhancement / external tasks)`.
2. Write `<STATE_DIR>/step5-brief.md` from the template in [`dispatch-analyst.md`](dispatch-analyst.md) § Step 5.
3. Split into parts of ≤ 8 tasks in document order; dispatch ALL parts in ONE message (two-line prompts pointing at the brief). Print `↳ 5 task sheets <k>/<n> parts` as parts return — relay each part's one-line summary, not its findings in full.
4. Check each part file, retry rules per the dispatch file.
5. Write `<STATE_DIR>/step5.json` = `{parts: [...], failed_tasks: [...]}`.

## Step 6 — Consultant review (optional)

1. Print the Step 6 line. Ask the review question of [`dispatch-review.md`](dispatch-review.md) § Step 6. Skip → print `(skipped — user choice)` and go to Step 7.
2. Dispatch one consultant per module in scope in ONE message. Each writes `<STATE_DIR>/step6.<M>.json` and returns one line; print `↳ 6 review <M> done`.
3. Handle `objections` per the dispatch file.

## Step 7 — Assemble the model (main thread)

1. Print the Step 7 line. Run `assemble-model.mjs`, then `build-process-doc.mjs --check`, per [`dispatch-review.md`](dispatch-review.md) § Step 7.

## Step 8 — Build HTML (main thread)

1. Print the Step 8 line.
2. `node "<PLUGIN_ROOT>/scripts/process/build-process-doc.mjs" "<STATE_DIR>/process-model.json" --out-dir "<PROC_DIR>"` (`--same-version` to rebuild the current version, `--major` for a new major version; a review run after a skipped one is a new minor version).
3. Relay the builder's warnings grouped by kind (≤ 10 lines), then the JSON result (`html`, `version`, `warnings`). Errors → fix and rebuild once; still failing → STOP and report.

### Step 8b — English companion (unless `<lang>` is `en` or the user opts out)

1. `node "<PLUGIN_ROOT>/scripts/process/companion.mjs" texts "<STATE_DIR>/process-model.json" --out "<STATE_DIR>/texts-en.json" --chunks <n>` — `n` = ceil(items / 750). Prose only, de-duplicated; codes and SAP identifiers are never extracted.
2. Write `<STATE_DIR>/translate-brief.md` from the template in [`dispatch-review.md`](dispatch-review.md) § Step 8b; dispatch `n` `sap-writer` (`model: "sonnet"`) in ONE message, each with a two-line prompt (`Translate chunk <file>. Follow the brief exactly: <brief>`). Each writes `<chunk>.en.json` and returns one line.
3. `node "<PLUGIN_ROOT>/scripts/process/companion.mjs" apply "<STATE_DIR>/process-model.json" <every .en.json> --lang en --out "<STATE_DIR>/process-model.en.json"` — exit code 3 = untranslated items: re-dispatch the chunk(s) holding them once.
4. Build it like Step 8 with `--as-version <primary version>` (`… build-process-doc.mjs "<STATE_DIR>/process-model.en.json" --out-dir "<PROC_DIR>" --as-version <ver>`) → `<MODULE>-process-v<ver>-en.html`.

## Step 9 — Validation + handoff

1. Print the Step 9 line.
2. Check (read the model, not the HTML):
   - every confirmed entry point of `attach.json` (minus `excluded`) appears in some row's `tcodes` / variant, or in `step4.json → unplaced` — list the missing ones

# Translate brief — process map companion (ko → en)

You translate one chunk of the prose of an SAP process map from Korean to English for SAP module consultants.

## Input / output
- Input: the chunk file named in your prompt: `{ "from": "ko", "to": "", "items": [{ "i": <n>, "text": "<ko>" }] }`
- Output: write `<same path with .json replaced by .en.json>` (UTF-8, with node or the Write tool):
  `{ "items": [{ "i": <n>, "text": "<en>" }] }` — EVERY input item exactly once, same `i`, nothing else.
- Check the file parses and the item count equals the input count:
  `node -e "const a=require(process.argv[1]),b=require(process.argv[2]);if(a.items.length!==b.items.length)process.exit(1)" <in> <out>`
- Return ONLY: `TRANSLATED <in file> items=<n> file=<out file>`.

## Rules
- Plain, short declarative English; consultant register. Keep the meaning exactly; do not add or drop facts.
- Keep SAP identifiers, programs, tables, fields, TCodes, BAPIs, codes, numbers and units literal (`ZMMM20560`, `EKKO-ZZCONTTYPE`, `ME21N`, `1100`, `D1`).
- Standard SAP terms in their usual English: 구매요청 = purchase requisition, 구매오더 = purchase order, 입고 = goods receipt, 출고 = goods issue, 송장 = invoice, 정보레코드 = info record, 구매처 = vendor, 자재 = material, 플랜트 = plant, 저장위치 = storage location, 법인 = company / entity, 법인간 = intercompany, 판매오더 = sales order, 청구 = billing, 상계 = netting, 재고이전 = stock transfer, 승인 = release (documents) / approval (people), 확인필요 = to be confirmed, (추정) = (estimated).
- Keep markup: `**bold**`, backticks, "\n" line breaks, "→", brackets.
- Region tags like [KR] [GL] [SG] stay as they are.
- No people's names; if one appears, keep it as is (do not invent).

content.content:
---
name: Entire-Checkpoint trailer in every commit
description: When making git commits in sc4sap_project, MUST include `Entire-Checkpoint: <id>` trailer to keep entire session tracking intact
type: feedback
originSessionId: 21e03650-294e-4f69-aaef-74c569183474
modified: 2026-09-29T23:29:06.682Z
---
When creating any `git commit` in `sc4sap_project` (or any repo where `entire` is enabled), the commit message MUST include an `Entire-Checkpoint: <id>` trailer in the trailer block (next to / below `Co-Authored-By:`).

**Why:** `entire attach <session-id>` only registers checkpoint metadata in entire's DB and prints "Copy to your commit message to attach: Entire-Checkpoint: <id>". It does NOT automatically amend the commit to add the trailer (because last commit may already be pushed). The trailer is the chain mechanism — without it on a commit, entire's session ↔ commit linkage breaks for that commit and every subsequent one in the chain.

**How to apply:**
- Before authoring a commit, run `entire sessions list` (or `entire status`) and grab the active session's `checkpoint <id>` field.

세 가지 모두 끝냈어요.

**1. GetGuiStatus 확인 — 통과**
- 재시작 후 HKT-DEV의 ZSDM50040으로 확인했어요.
- `function_codes` + `compact`를 주면 한 줄만 나와요. 예: TRANS = Transfer, F13, 툴바.
- `status_name`을 주면 그 Status만 나오고, TIT/DOC 같은 다른 정보는 빠져요.
- 남은 점: Status 하나만 골라도 텍스트 없는 ALV 표준 기능이 다 딸려 와서 여전히 길어요. 그래서 문구 작업은 `function_codes`로만 조회했어요.

**2. MM 버튼 문구 — MM v2.2 빌드 (ko + en)**
- 182건 중 114건은 화면의 실제 문구로 바꿨어요. 예: `'Create PO'(CREATE)`.
- 10건은 SM30 저장, F8, ME55, MR21처럼 표준 조작이라 "(문구 추정)" 표시만 지웠어요.
- 58건은 표시를 그대로 뒀어요. 이유는 셋이에요.
  - 그 코드가 GUI Status에 없거나 문구가 비어 있어요.
  - 단계에 버튼 코드가 아예 안 적혀 있어요.
  - ZMMR50061 같은 몇 개는 SAP 안에서 조회가 실패해요(`RS_CUA_INTERNAL_FETCH sy-subrc=1`). 필터 문제는 아니에요.
- 영어판은 새로 생긴 문구 127건만 번역했어요. 버튼 문구는 원문 그대로 뒀어요.
- SD v1.1과 SD-MM 통합 맵은 같은 버전으로 다시 빌드했어요. 이제 MM v2.2를 가리켜요.
- 건드린 파일은 모두 `.bak-gui`로 백업해 뒀어요.

**3. MCP 커밋 — `7f66e27`**
- 레포가 `main`에 있어서 새 브랜치 `feat/getguistatus-filter`를 만들어 커밋했어요.
- 들어간 건 GetGuiStatus 파일 7개뿐이에요. dump-feed 변경은 커밋하지 않고 그대로 뒀어요.
- 처음 커밋은 pre-commit의 biome 검사에서 막혔어요. `cuaFilter.ts`의 forEach 하나를 고치고 다시 빌드한 뒤, 실행 중인 캐시에도 복사했어요. 단위 테스트 5개가 통과해요.
- 실수가 하나 있었어요. 커밋이 실패한 직후 `entire attach -f`를 실행해서, 이미 푸시된 c9461c6에 걸렸어요. 확인해 보니 그 커밋에는 원래 같은 체크포인트가 있어서 바뀐 건 없어요. HEAD는 그대로 `origin/main`과 같아요.
- 푸시, main 머지, npm 배포는 하지 않았어요. 필요하면 말씀해 주세요.

**Why:** user asked to update all npm deps and publish + vendor. **How to apply:** next vendor work starts from 4.8.13 / c9461c6. See [[reference-mcp-repo-npm-test-hits-sap]], [[reference_sc4sap_source_locations]].
description: "In abap-mcp-adt-powerup, plain `npm test` runs SAP integration tests that create/update/delete objects; unit-only command given here"

In `~/.claude/plugins/marketplaces/abap-mcp-adt-powerup`, `npm test` = `jest --passWithNoTests` with no ignore list, so it runs `src/__tests__/integration/**` and `admin/shared-deps/**` too. Those connect through `tests/test-config.yaml` → `environment.env` (`~/Documents/mcp-abap-adt/sessions/S4H.env`) and create, update and delete classes / programs / BDEFs in `$TMP` (cleanup_after: true). Happened 2026-10-20; stopped mid-run, log showed every created object deleted.

Unit tests only (34 suites, 410 tests, no SAP, ~1 min):
`npx jest --testPathIgnorePatterns=integration --testPathIgnorePatterns=admin --testPathIgnorePatterns=/dist/`

Also: jest 30.5 adds `@parcel/watcher`, whose install script fails there (nested jest tree, path > 260 chars, cmd.exe ENOENT) — jest pinned at 30.2. Release build (`npm run build` / prepublishOnly) runs `biome check --write` on src. Related: [[feedback-destructive-test-preapproval]], [[feedback-verify-before-publish]].
description: Default to local verification (npm pack + install locally, smoke test) before any destructive or public-facing action like npm publish, git push to main, marketplace release
type: feedback
originSessionId: 44e18665-d223-475a-83dc-c08cd0bfcd54
When offered a choice between "just ship it, unit tests passed" and "verify locally first (npm pack → install → smoke test on real system) then ship", the user **always picks verify-first**.

**Why:** The user is cautious about irreversible public actions (npm publish has ~24h unpublish window, git push to main can't be silently undone, marketplace release affects other users). Unit tests use mocks and may miss real-environment shape mismatches. User explicitly said "무섭다" (it's scary) when a git-push plan was laid out without a verification lap first.

**How to apply:**
- For any flow ending in `npm publish`, `git push`, `gh release`, marketplace release, or similar: insert a local verification step **first** and present it as the default path. Do not ask the user to "pick A or B" if one option is a verify-first path — propose verify-first and confirm.
- Local verification pattern for npm libs: `npm pack` in source → install tarball into the consuming project → rebuild consumer → smoke test in the real target system (e.g. actual SAP ECC) before publishing.
- Local verification pattern for git pushes: confirm branch state + remote state + diff against remote before pushing; for destructive remote ops (force push, branch delete, backup-and-replace), pause and explicitly enumerate what will happen.
- If the user is already stressed (e.g. "무섭다", "걱정된다"), acknowledge briefly and lead with the safer path — don't enumerate multiple options again.

## [Unreleased]

## [4.8.13] - 2026-10-20

### Added
- **`GetSmartFormLayout`** (read-only, on-premise and legacy systems): page and window layout of a SmartForm. Per page the format, orientation, next page, CPI / LPI and style; per window its type (MAIN, SECONDARY, ...), position and size as stored (value + unit) and converted to millimetres (CM, MM, IN, PT, TW, and LN / CH through the page LPI / CPI). Reads the active version (a form that was never activated is read from its saved version and `active` is false). `language` takes a 1-character SAP key or a 2-letter ISO code. Layout only: no texts, code or form interface. Runs through `ZMCP_ADT_DISPATCH` action `SSF_LAYOUT`, so it works on the OData backend (BASIS 7.40) and over SOAP RFC (BASIS 7.31). Needs the new `ZMCP_SSF_LAYOUT` FM and the `SSF_LAYOUT` dispatcher branch; without them the tool answers with an install hint.
- **`GetSmartFormContent`** (read-only, on-premise and legacy systems): what a SmartForm prints, for preview rendering. Per page and window (position in mm) the content tree: text nodes with their lines (paragraph format, inline character formats, `&symbols&`), include texts, templates with line heights and cells (width, border widths, shading colour), loops and tables with header / footer events, graphics, addresses, print conditions; code nodes only as markers, never program lines. Also the form interface and global data with their types (`data`), the SmartStyles as CSS, SE78 graphics with a fixed key as BMP with their printed size, and include texts with a fixed key. Everything is written under the MCP output directory (`smartforms/<form>/`, full result in `<form>.content.json`); `summary: true` answers with an overview (windows, data declarations, `&symbols&`, graphics, files) because the full tree easily exceeds a tool answer. Runs through `ZMCP_ADT_DISPATCH` action `SSF_CONTENT` (FM `ZMCP_SSF_CONTENT`).
- **`RenderSmartForm`** (on-premise and legacy systems): the output of a SmartForm exactly as SAP prints it, for given interface values. Calls the form's generated function module with GETOTF (no dialog, no print, no spool) and writes the OTF and the PDF under the MCP output directory (`smartforms/<form>/<form>.sap.otf.txt` / `.sap.pdf`). `values` / `values_file` take the interface in internal format; `device` or `families` choose the device type, so the output has the printer fonts the form was made for. The form's own program lines run as in a real print and may read the database — pass invented sample values only. Runs through `ZMCP_ADT_DISPATCH` action `SSF_RENDER` (FM `ZMCP_SSF_RENDER`); without them the tool answers with an install hint.
- **`CreateSmartForm`** (writes, on-premise and legacy systems, DEV profiles only): creates — or with `overwrite` replaces — a Z/Y SmartForm from Form Builder XML (the format of SMARTFORMS > Utilities > Download and of `GetSmartFormContent`'s form XML). The form is checked and stored active, its function module generated (also for a replaced form); when the check finds errors it is stored inactive and the errors come back. `package_name` defaults to `$TMP`; another package needs `transport_request`. The XML travels raw-deflate compressed in parts of 5000 base64 characters, because the OData `Dispatch` function import carries its parameters in the URL. Runs through `ZMCP_ADT_DISPATCH` action `SSF_UPLOAD_XML` (FM `ZMCP_SSF_UPLOAD`); without them the tool answers with an install hint.
- **`DeleteSmartForm`** (writes, destructive, DEV profiles only): deletes a Z/Y SmartForm of a local package (`$TMP`, `$…`) with its generated function module — a dry run unless `confirm: true`; transportable forms are refused. Runs through action `SSF_DELETE_FORM` (FM `ZMCP_SSF_DELETE`).
- **`GetSmartFormContent`** reads more of what decides the print:
  - SmartStyle paragraphs and character formats as stored (value + unit, family, size, tabs), with the SE73 bar-code definition (`barcodeDef`: symbology, module, height) of bar-code formats.
  - Table / template patterns with their outer frame flag (`frame.border`), box sides switched on with thickness 0 (`on`), and the `reference` of a template line type that takes another line's height.
  - Styles named only in output options (template / window STDSTYLE) are read too.
  - The device type and its printer fonts for the form's families (`printer`).
  - Texts with no translation in the logon language are taken from the form's master language, as SAP prints them. This needs `ZMCP_SSF_CONTENT` with `IV_LANGUAGE` for the `FORM` part; an older FM keeps the logon-language texts.

### Fixed
- `npm run docs:tools` cut a description at the first quote of the other kind (`'… (e.g. "ZMY_FORM")'`, `"… dump's …"`): string values now end at the quote they opened with, escapes are resolved. The user-guide tool lists are regenerated with the full texts.

### Changed
- Dependencies updated within their major versions: `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` 1.32.1, `axios` 1.20, `fast-xml-parser` 5.11, `zod` 4.6, `js-yaml` 4.3, `pino` 10.4, `pino-pretty` 13.2, and the dev tooling (Biome 2.5, ts-jest, tsx, express, yaml). `jest` stays on 30.2: 30.5 pulls in `@parcel/watcher`, whose install script fails under the nested `jest` tree on Windows (path over 260 characters).

## [Unreleased]

## [4.8.14] - 2026-10-28

### Changed
- **`GetGuiStatus`** answers with only what was asked for. `status_name` used to narrow the status list alone, so a large program interface still came back whole (15K+ tokens). It now narrows every table to that status: its SET functions, FUN texts, PFK keys, BUT toolbar and ACT / MEN / MTX menus; TIT / DOC / BIV are left out.
  - New `function_codes`: keep only these function codes (narrows FUN / SET / PFK / BUT).
  - New `format: "compact"`: `{ statuses: [{ code, type, functions: [{ code, text, icon?, fkey?, toolbar? }] }] }` — one line per function. `full` (default) keeps the CUA tables.
  - A status still lists the empty-text ALV standard functions it copies; pass `function_codes` when you need a few captions.

  - 버전을 4.8.14로 올렸어요.

  - 단위 테스트 35개 묶음(415개)이 통과했어요. SAP에 붙는 통합 테스트는 돌리지 않았어요.
  - 릴리스 빌드와 biome 검사도 통과했어요.

  - SAP 실제 확인은 이 네트워크로 바꾸기 전에 HKT-DEV에서 같은 코드로 이미 했어요.

originSessionId: 624e4d17-84e6-4cca-a52f-34db7cd7ad7e
---
User authors the sc4sap plugin. When patching plugin code (bridge, scripts, hooks, skills), THREE locations must stay in sync:

1. **Project source (distribution source-of-truth)** — `C:/Users/pssps/Documents/Projects/sc4sap_project/sc4sap/`
   - This is what gets published to the marketplace.
   - All new fixes MUST land here first (for git/CHANGELOG).
2. **Marketplace copy (install-time source)** — `C:/Users/pssps/.claude/plugins/marketplaces/sc4sap/`
   - What Claude Code ships into the cache when the plugin is enabled/updated.
3. **Cache (runtime)** — `C:/Users/pssps/.claude/plugins/cache/sc4sap/sc4sap/<version>/`
   - What actually runs. A fresh plugin install copies from marketplace → cache, overwriting ad-hoc patches here.

**Patching workflow**:
- Edit project source first.
- Mirror to marketplace (for install-time correctness).
- Mirror to cache (to take effect in the running session — otherwise user must `/reload-plugins` or restart).
- `diff` all three at the end — they should match exactly.

**Why not just cache?** Cache is blown away on plugin update. Project source drives git + publish; marketplace is the Claude Code-facing source.

**Related**: `bridge/mcp-server.cjs` previously only checked legacy `<project>/.sc4sap/sap.env` and `<plugin>/.sc4sap/sap.env`, missing the multi-profile path (`<project>/.sc4sap/active-profile.txt` → `~/.sc4sap/profiles/<alias>/sap.env`). Patched 2026-04-21 in all three locations to resolve via active-profile first, with legacy paths as fallback.

**Which `<version>` folder runs (2026-10-14):** Claude Code launches the folder named by `installPath` in `~/.claude/plugins/installed_plugins.json` (user scope), not the newest-looking folder name. Until 2026-10-14 it pointed at `0.6.14`, whose *contents* had been synced up to 0.6.35 / MCP 4.8.12, while folders `0.6.32`/`0.6.34`/`0.6.35` were older or had no vendor. On 2026-10-14 it was renamed: `0.6.35` = copy of the running folder + HEAD `c4d5d21` overlay, registry now points to `0.6.35` (backups: `installed_plugins.json.bak-20261014`, `cache/.../0.6.35.bak-20261014`; old `0.6.14` kept for rollback). Mirror target = the folder in `installPath`; check it before every sync and after a version bump.
originSessionId: d0295105-8a83-493b-9c14-d5e48ffe7fad
---
**Where Claude Code `/plugin` reads "latest version" from:**

- `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` → `version` (1 field)
- `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` → `plugins[0].version` (1 field)
- `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` → root `version` (1 field)

**Not** from `package.json`. `package.json.version` is for npm-side consumption only.

**Cache behavior:**
- Installed plugins live at `~/.claude/plugins/cache/sc4sap/sc4sap/<version>/` — keyed by the marketplace version string
- When the marketplace manifest shows a new version, Claude Code auto-downloads into a fresh `<new-version>/` dir
- No manual cache patching needed on version bump — only the .claude-plugin manifests

**Incident (2026-04-24):** All three version fields were stuck at `0.6.5` across the 0.6.6 → 0.6.11 release cycle, so `/plugin` kept reporting 0.6.5 as latest even after package.json moved to 0.6.11. Fixed in PR #40 (commit `baf676b`).

**Automated safeguard added in same PR:** `tests/validation/plugin-structure.test.ts` now cross-checks all three .claude-plugin version fields against `package.json.version`. Future drift fails CI at the `verify · typecheck · test` step.

**How to apply:** At every release, bump `package.json.version` AND all three `.claude-plugin/*.json` version fields together. The new CI test will flag it if you miss, but don't rely on that — do it in one commit.
originSessionId: 0f8d75a1-19fc-415f-890e-3d9ef52c9de8
---
**Changed 2026-04-24.** The `active` branch at https://github.com/babamba2/superclaude-for-sap is now a collaboration branch — the user confirmed at least two sources push to it (different claude sessions + potentially other contributors). Observed evidence: during the 0.6.11 work, origin/active received `894c5be Merge branch 'main' into active` from a paek-authored commit while this session was composing a local commit, triggering a non-fast-forward push rejection.

**Why:** the earlier assumption that force-push + amend was safe on active (treated as the user's personal dev branch) is now wrong; treat active with the same discipline as main.

**How to apply:**

1. **NEVER** use `git push --force` or `--force-with-lease` on active. If a push is rejected, fetch + rebase (for unpushed local commits) or merge (if remote commits need to be preserved).
2. **NEVER** use `git commit --amend` on a commit that has been pushed to active.
3. **Rebase is allowed only on unpushed local commits** — e.g., `git rebase origin/active` to linearize local work before first push is fine, since no one else sees those commits yet.
4. **The Entire-Checkpoint attach workflow (`entire attach <sid> --force` + `git push --force-with-lease`) is not used**. Attach now runs automatically at session start via the `SessionStart` hook in `~/.claude/settings.json` (`entire hooks claude-code session-start`).
5. **Direct pushes to main remain prohibited** — changes flow active → PR → main as before.
6. When a push is rejected with non-fast-forward:
   - `git fetch origin active`
   - Inspect `git log HEAD..origin/active` to see what landed

# SuperClaude for SAP (sc4sap) — Development Rules

This file is the **index** of development rules — NOT a payload to preload. Detailed rules live in `common/` and `exceptions/`. Consult files on demand per [`common/context-loading-protocol.md`](common/context-loading-protocol.md) — 4-tier model: **Tier 1** global mandatory safety baseline (always loaded by every agent: `data-extraction-policy`, `sap-version-reference`, `naming-conventions`; `context-loading-protocol` + `model-routing-rule` are orchestrator-only, read by skills), **Tier 2** role-mandatory per agent group, **Tier 3** triggered reads, **Tier 4** per-task kit. Everything referenced below is MANDATORY for every sc4sap session (agents, skills, direct user requests, pipelines).

## Development Standards — References

| Topic | Reference |
|---|---|
| Naming conventions (Z/Y prefixes, module prefix, includes, FGs, tables, DEs, DOs) | [`common/naming-conventions.md`](common/naming-conventions.md) |
| Field typing priority (Standard DE → CBO DE → new CBO DE → Data Type+Length; never `LIFNR CHAR 10`) | [`common/field-typing-rule.md`](common/field-typing-rule.md) |
| Function Module source convention (inline IMPORTING/EXPORTING/TABLES in FUNCTION statement; no placeholder, no shadow locals) | [`common/function-module-rule.md`](common/function-module-rule.md) |
| SAP version awareness (ECC vs S/4HANA — tables, TCodes, BAPIs, patterns) | [`common/sap-version-reference.md`](common/sap-version-reference.md) |
| ABAP release awareness (syntax availability per release, never emit newer features than `ABAP_RELEASE`) | [`common/abap-release-reference.md`](common/abap-release-reference.md) |
| Clean ABAP coding standards (paradigm-split) | shared baseline [`common/clean-code.md`](common/clean-code.md) + one of [`common/clean-code-oop.md`](common/clean-code-oop.md) or [`common/clean-code-procedural.md`](common/clean-code-procedural.md) chosen from the Phase 1B Paradigm dimension; also pulls in `constant-rule.md`, `text-element-rule.md`, `abap-release-reference.md` |
| Procedural FORM naming (screen-bound suffix) | [`common/procedural-form-naming.md`](common/procedural-form-naming.md) |
| OOP two-class split pattern | [`common/oop-pattern.md`](common/oop-pattern.md) |
| Include structure (Main + conditional includes) | [`common/include-structure.md`](common/include-structure.md) |
| ALV display rules | [`common/alv-rules.md`](common/alv-rules.md) |
| Tabstrip screens (STRIP_CTRL + subscreen area + tab PUSH rows, `CALL SUBSCREEN` in PBO and PAI) | [`common/screen-tabstrip.md`](common/screen-tabstrip.md) |
| OK_CODE binding pattern (one TOP variable + screen NAME + PAI dispatch; never `CASE sy-ucomm`) | [`common/ok-code-pattern.md`](common/ok-code-pattern.md) |
| SPRO lookup protocol (consultant agents, IMG/Customizing) | [`common/spro-lookup.md`](common/spro-lookup.md) |
| Customization lookup protocol (existing Z*/Y* BAdI impl, CMOD, form-exits, appends — mandatory before recommending new enhancements/extensions) | [`common/customization-lookup.md`](common/customization-lookup.md) |
| Data extraction policy (blocklist rule, `acknowledge_risk` hard rule, refusal template) | [`common/data-extraction-policy.md`](common/data-extraction-policy.md) |
| Transport client rule (every `CreateTransport` must receive explicit `client` from `.sc4sap/sap.env` SAP_CLIENT — never an implicit default) | [`common/transport-client-rule.md`](common/transport-client-rule.md) |
| Blocklist (per-category table lists) | [`exceptions/table_exception.md`](exceptions/table_exception.md) (index) + `exceptions/*.md` section files |
| Industry business-context references (14 industries) | [`industry/README.md`](industry/README.md) + `industry/*.md` |
| Country / localization references (16 countries + EU common) | [`country/README.md`](country/README.md) + `country/*.md` |
| Active modules — cross-module integration matrix (MM↔PS, SD↔CO, QM↔PP, …) | [`common/active-modules.md`](common/active-modules.md) |
| Context loading protocol (CLAUDE.md is an index; every dispatch declares its minimal context kit) | [`common/context-loading-protocol.md`](common/context-loading-protocol.md) |
| Model routing (Opus for judgment / novel code; Sonnet for template + bulk writes; Haiku `sap-checker` fan-out for fetch / verify / detect) | [`common/model-routing-rule.md`](common/model-routing-rule.md) |
| Model dispatch mode (`auto` default = route per rule; `user-defined` = ask Opus / Sonnet / Haiku before each dispatch group; set via `/sc4sap:sap-option`) | [`common/model-dispatch-mode.md`](common/model-dispatch-mode.md) |
| Cost mode (`standard` default = current behavior; `eco` = cheaper sub-agent models and effort, low main-thread effort, same deliverable; set via `/sc4sap:sap-option` or one-off `/sc4sap:eco`) | [`common/cost-mode.md`](common/cost-mode.md) |

Before any work: verify `.sc4sap/config.json` exists and contains `sapVersion`, `abapRelease`, `industry`. Every recommendation, piece of generated code, and tool invocation must respect those fields.

## Critical Rules (summary — full text in referenced files)

1. **Custom objects use `Z`/`Y` prefix.** Full rules: `common/naming-conventions.md`.
2. **Match SAP version and ABAP release.** Never use S/4-only tables on ECC or syntax newer than the configured `abapRelease`. Full rules: `common/sap-version-reference.md`, `common/abap-release-reference.md`.
3. **Transport discipline.** Every change goes on a transport. Description format: `[MODULE] [Action] [Object] - [brief]`. Never release with syntax errors or inactive objects. Every `CreateTransport` call must receive an explicit `client` parameter resolved from `.sc4sap/sap.env` SAP_CLIENT (full rule: `common/transport-client-rule.md`).
4. **Activate after every change.** Run `GetAbapSemanticAnalysis` for syntax, then `GetInactiveObjects` to confirm no leftovers. Follow Clean ABAP conventions: `common/clean-code.md` (shared) + the paradigm-specific companion (`clean-code-oop.md` OR `clean-code-procedural.md`).
5. **Data extraction is gated.** Before any `GetTableContents` / `GetSqlQuery`: consult `exceptions/table_exception.md` and `common/data-extraction-policy.md`. Schema/DDIC (`GetTable`, `GetStructure`, `GetView`, `GetDataElement`, `GetDomain`) is always allowed.
6. **`acknowledge_risk` requires explicit user affirmative** (`yes` / `승인` / `authorize` / `approve` / `proceed` / `confirmed`). Ambiguous commands (`뽑아봐`, `try it`, `pull it`, `my mistake`) are NOT authorization. Per-call, per-table, per-session — never carries over. Full protocol: `common/data-extraction-policy.md` → "The `acknowledge_risk` Parameter — HARD RULE".
7. **Industry context matters.** For config analysis / business process design / Fit-Gap: load the project's `industry/<key>.md` (from `config.json` → `industry` or `sap.env` → `SAP_INDUSTRY`). If unset, ask the user.
8. **Country / localization context matters.** For tax, e-invoicing, banking, statutory reporting, date/number formats: load the project's `country/<iso>.md` (from `config.json` → `country` or `sap.env` → `SAP_COUNTRY`, ISO alpha-2 lowercase: `kr`, `us`, `de`, `eu-common`, …). Multi-country projects load every relevant file and flag cross-country touchpoints (intercompany, intra-EU VAT, transfer pricing). If unset, ask the user.

Enforcement: L1 agent instructions → L2 this file → L3 `PreToolUse` hook (`scripts/hooks/block-forbidden-tables.mjs`) → L4 MCP server upstream guard.

## Plugin Usage

### Skills (`/sc4sap:` prefix)
- `/sc4sap:setup` — Initial plugin setup + SPRO config generation (auto-invokes `trust-session`)
- `/sc4sap:create-program` — Full ABAP program pipeline (Phase 0–8) with execution-mode gate (auto/manual/hybrid) and parallel Phase 4/6; auto-invokes `trust-session` at Phase 1
- `/sc4sap:create-object` — Single ABAP object creation (auto-invokes `trust-session`)
- `/sc4sap:program-to-spec` — Reverse-engineer a program into a spec artifact
- `/sc4sap:program-to-manual` — End-user manual for one program: one HTML file, scenario steps on drawn screens with numbered callouts, check points, field reference, messages & actions, glossary, revision history; one step per A4 landscape page in print. Output `.sc4sap/manuals/<PROGRAM>-v<n>-<lang>.html` (auto-invokes `trust-session`)
- `/sc4sap:analyze-code` — Static code review (auto-invokes `trust-session`)
- `/sc4sap:compare-programs` — Business-angle side-by-side comparison of 2–5 ABAP programs sharing the same scenario but differing by module / country / persona (reader = consultant) → one editable, versioned HTML report (verdict matrix + *Differences only*, field differences, screens side by side, decision guide, English companion) `comparisons/<NAME>-v<n>-<lang>.html` under the profile artifact base (auto-invokes `trust-session`)

| Model dispatch mode (`auto` default = route per rule; `user-defined` = ask Opus / Sonnet / Haiku before each dispatch group; set via `/sc4sap:sap-option`) | [`common/model-dispatch-mode.md`](common/model-dispatch-mode.md) |

Before any work: verify `.sc4sap/config.json` exists and contains `sapVersion`, `abapRelease`, `industry`. Every recommendation, piece of generated code, and tool invocation must respect those fields.

## Critical Rules (summary — full text in referenced files)

1. **Custom objects use `Z`/`Y` prefix.** Full rules: `common/naming-conventions.md`.
2. **Match SAP version and ABAP release.** Never use S/4-only tables on ECC or syntax newer than the configured `abapRelease`. Full rules: `common/sap-version-reference.md`, `common/abap-release-reference.md`.
3. **Transport discipline.** Every change goes on a transport. Description format: `[MODULE] [Action] [Object] - [brief]`. Never release with syntax errors or inactive objects. Every `CreateTransport` call must receive an explicit `client` parameter resolved from `.sc4sap/sap.env` SAP_CLIENT (full rule: `common/transport-client-rule.md`).
4. **Activate after every change.** Run `GetAbapSemanticAnalysis` for syntax, then `GetInactiveObjects` to confirm no leftovers. Follow Clean ABAP conventions: `common/clean-code.md` (shared) + the paradigm-specific companion (`clean-code-oop.md` OR `clean-code-procedural.md`).
5. **Data extraction is gated.** Before any `GetTableContents` / `GetSqlQuery`: consult `exceptions/table_exception.md` and `common/data-extraction-policy.md`. Schema/DDIC (`GetTable`, `GetStructure`, `GetView`, `GetDataElement`, `GetDomain`) is always allowed.
6. **`acknowledge_risk` requires explicit user affirmative** (`yes` / `승인` / `authorize` / `approve` / `proceed` / `confirmed`). Ambiguous commands (`뽑아봐`, `try it`, `pull it`, `my mistake`) are NOT authorization. Per-call, per-table, per-session — never carries over. Full protocol: `common/data-extraction-policy.md` → "The `acknowledge_risk` Parameter — HARD RULE".
7. **Industry context matters.** For config analysis / business process design / Fit-Gap: load the project's `industry/<key>.md` (from `config.json` → `industry` or `sap.env` → `SAP_INDUSTRY`). If unset, ask the user.
8. **Country / localization context matters.** For tax, e-invoicing, banking, statutory reporting, date/number formats: load the project's `country/<iso>.md` (from `config.json` → `country` or `sap.env` → `SAP_COUNTRY`, ISO alpha-2 lowercase: `kr`, `us`, `de`, `eu-common`, …). Multi-country projects load every relevant file and flag cross-country touchpoints (intercompany, intra-EU VAT, transfer pricing). If unset, ask the user.

Enforcement: L1 agent instructions → L2 this file → L3 `PreToolUse` hook (`scripts/hooks/block-forbidden-tables.mjs`) → L4 MCP server upstream guard.

## Plugin Usage

### Skills (`/sc4sap:` prefix)
- `/sc4sap:setup` — Initial plugin setup + SPRO config generation (auto-invokes `trust-session`)
- `/sc4sap:create-program` — Full ABAP program pipeline (Phase 0–8) with execution-mode gate (auto/manual/hybrid) and parallel Phase 4/6; auto-invokes `trust-session` at Phase 1
- `/sc4sap:create-object` — Single ABAP object creation (auto-invokes `trust-session`)
- `/sc4sap:program-to-spec` — Reverse-engineer a program into a spec artifact
- `/sc4sap:program-to-manual` — End-user manual for one program: one HTML file, scenario steps on drawn screens with numbered callouts, check points, field reference, messages & actions, glossary, revision history; one step per A4 landscape page in print. Output `.sc4sap/manuals/<PROGRAM>-v<n>-<lang>.html` (auto-invokes `trust-session`)
- `/sc4sap:analyze-code` — Static code review (auto-invokes `trust-session`)
- `/sc4sap:compare-programs` — Business-angle side-by-side comparison of 2–5 ABAP programs sharing the same scenario but differing by module / country / persona (reader = consultant) → one editable, versioned HTML report (verdict matrix + *Differences only*, field differences, screens side by side, decision guide, English companion) `comparisons/<NAME>-v<n>-<lang>.html` under the profile artifact base (auto-invokes `trust-session`)
- `/sc4sap:config-to-document` — One module's configuration documented from the live system: IMG tree, per IMG activity the real table values drawn on an SM30-style screen, customer-changed rows with their transports, configuration checks, SAP IMG documentation, consultant notes written by the module consultant agent and reviewed by `sap-critic` → one HTML file `config-docs/<MODULE>/<MODULE>-config-v<n>-<lang>.html` under the profile artifact base. MM first.
- `/sc4sap:interface-mapping-spec` — Interface mapping specification as one editable HTML page in the classic template layout (cover, revision history, header, Source → Target grid with R / MAPPING, optional synchronous response block, conversion rules, extraction condition, field guide). SAP side read from DDIC / FM signature or, for new interfaces, from a `TABLE-FIELD` list or the module consultant's proposal; counterpart fields, DB types, conversion rules and scenario defaults proposed; in-page checks; versioned with English companion → `interfaces/<IF_ID>/<IF_ID>-v<n>-<lang>.html` under the profile artifact base
- `/sc4sap:smartform-preview` — Expected print of one SmartForm without a print program: `GetSmartFormContent` (form XML, SmartStyle CSS, SE78 graphics) → windows drawn at their mm positions with templates, loops (sample rows) and graphics; `&fields&` filled with invented sample values sized to the DDIC types; report of cut-off cells / windows → `smartforms/<FORM>/<FORM>-preview.{jpg,html}` + `values.json` under the profile artifact base. Read-only.
- `/sc4sap:smartform-from-pdf` — SmartForm from a PDF (or screenshot) of a printed form: `read-pdf` (texts / rules / images in mm) → `plan-form` (rules → templates, texts in the formats of existing SmartStyles — no style is created) → fields, item loops and interface decided with the user (`shape-form`) → `write-form` (Form Builder XML) → `CreateSmartForm` on DEV → `RenderSmartForm` → `compare-layout` score against the source page → `smartforms/<FORM>/` under the profile artifact base. Writes (DEV only).
- `/sc4sap:analyze-symptom` — Dump/error root-cause analysis (auto-invokes `trust-session`)
- `/sc4sap:analyze-cbo-obj` — Inventory a CBO package → save frequently-used Z objects to `.sc4sap/cbo/<MODULE>/<PACKAGE>/` for reuse by `create-program` / `program-to-spec` (auto-invokes `trust-session`)
- `/sc4sap:module-to-process` — One editable HTML process map per module (or process area), built only from the TCodes users actually run (productive ST03N via `SAP_USAGE_RFCDEST`, or a saved / submitted usage list): used TCodes → programs → sources → reference graph → standard L1–L4 backbone (`configs/<M>/process-backbone.json`) → Opus hierarchy + PDD task sheets → optional module-consultant review → `assemble-model.mjs` → `build-process-doc.mjs` (BPH table, L3 scenario swimlanes, variant matrix, task sheets, appendix; edit mode + `--import`); optional BPH reconciliation (`bph-import.mjs`) and English companion (`companion.mjs`). Output `processes/<MODULE>/<MODULE>-process-v<ver>-<lang>.html` under the profile artifact base (auto-invokes `trust-session`)
- `/sc4sap:package-to-process` — redirect to `module-to-process` for one release
- `/sc4sap:ask-consultant` — Direct user-facing Q&A with a module consultant agent (SD/MM/FI/CO/PP/PS/PM/QM/TR/HCM/WM/TM/BW/Ariba/BC). Auto-routes by keywords, answers against the configured SAP environment. Read-only (no writes, no row extraction).
- `/sc4sap:mcp-setup` — MCP ABAP ADT server configuration guide
- `/sc4sap:sap-option` — View and edit `.sc4sap/sap.env` (credentials, industry, blocklist profile, HUD limits)
- `/sc4sap:sap-doctor` — Diagnose plugin / MCP / SAP connection health
- `/sc4sap:trust-session` — INTERNAL-ONLY — session-wide MCP permission bootstrap; direct invocation is rejected

### Agents
- Core: `sap-analyst`, `sap-architect`, `sap-code-reviewer`, `sap-critic`, `sap-debugger`, `sap-doc-specialist`, `sap-executor`, `sap-planner`, `sap-qa-tester`, `sap-writer`
- Checker: `sap-checker` — Haiku, read-only fan-out worker (`scout` / `verify` / `detect`) that returns structured lines; the main thread dispatches N of them and one Opus agent consumes the result. Used by `/sc4sap:create-program` Phase 1A scout, Phase 4 verification, Phase 6 `detect-judge`; `/sc4sap:analyze-code` size scout, large-object detect-judge, evidence verify; `/sc4sap:compare-programs` facts extraction; `/sc4sap:analyze-cbo-obj` + `/sc4sap:package-to-process` stocking scouts.
- Discovery: `sap-stocker` — CBO inventory / where-used graph / reusable object cataloging (Sonnet, R/O SAP + R/W on `.sc4sap/cbo/`). Consumed by `/sc4sap:analyze-cbo-obj`, `/sc4sap:create-program` (CBO reuse gate), and module consultants via their `<CBO_Stocking_Delegation>` block.

### SPRO Config Reference
`configs/{MODULE}/` contains `spro.md`, `tcodes.md`, `bapi.md`, `tables.md`, `enhancements.md`, `workflows.md` per module. Consultant agents consult these + `common/spro-lookup.md` before IMG answers.

### MCP Server (mcp-abap-adt)
All SAP interactions go through the MCP ABAP ADT server (150+ tools):
- CRUD: `CreateClass` / `UpdateClass` / `GetClass` / `DeleteClass` (and every DDIC/runtime object type)

- Runtime: `RunUnitTest`, `GetUnitTestResult`, `RuntimeAnalyzeDump`
- System: `GetTableContents`, `GetSqlQuery` (gated — see rule 5/6 above)
- Transport: `CreateTransport`, `GetTransport`, `ListTransports`
